title: Prelude in C major (BWV 846)
description: The opening prelude of The Well-Tempered Clavier, Book I: one broken-chord pattern repeated through a chain of rich harmonies. A perfect study in even sixteenths, quiet hands and listening to harmony change under your fingers.

arrangements.label: Intermediate
arrangements.notes: The complete 35-bar prelude as Bach wrote it; the only editorial choices are notating the held tenor note in bars 1-32 as a sixteenth tied to a dotted quarter so every voice fills the bar, and switching the right-hand staff to bass clef for the low arpeggio of bar 33 (back to treble in bar 34); in bars 33-35 both left-hand notes are struck together as whole notes.
teachingPoints: Learn the chord of each bar as a block first (bass, tenor, three right-hand notes), then unfold it into the sixteenth pattern.

Left hand: bass on the beat, tenor on the second sixteenth, both held while the right hand arpeggiates; where the tenor sits a 10th or more above the bass (bars 1, 4, 5, 9-15, 17, 20) release the bass early rather than stretching.
Hand-position shifts are marked at bars 1, 2, 5, 10, 16 and 19; the accidentals in bars 12, 14, 20, 22, 23, 28 and 32 define the colour of each harmony.
Bars 33-34 break the pattern with a long right-hand arpeggio over the low C and C/B struck together on the downbeat; practice them slowly and let the final chord in bar 35 ring.
